question: The presence of which of the following does NOT let the air passage in the respiratory system of humans collapse when there is less air in it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rings of cartilage**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rings of cartilage do not let the air pass in the respiratory system**
 
• **Rings of cartilage are present in the trachea and bronchi, and they prevent the airways from collapsing, **even when there is less air in them.
 
• These cartilaginous rings provide structural support to the respiratory system.
 
• These are C-shaped structures found in the trachea and bronchi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tendons**:

 
 
• Tendons are **connective tissues **that attach muscles to bones.
 
• They** help transmit force generated by muscles to move bones**.
 
 
 
• ​ **Ligaments:**
 
 
• Ligaments **are fibrous tissues that connect bones to other bones at joints.**
 
• They provide stability to joints by limiting movement.
 
• Ligaments do not play a role in maintaining the structure of the respiratory system.
 
 
 
• **Muscles**:
 
 
• Muscles in the **respiratory system, like the diaphragm and intercostal muscles, aid in breathing by expanding and contracting the chest cavity.**
 
• **They facilitate air movement in and out of the lungs.**
